target_identity: R2, Qwen3-derived, 28 layers, hidden 1024, 16 Q / 8 KV, head_dim 128, vocabulary 32768; exact weight hash required locally
historical_dependency: experiments/attention_shape/README.md and src/variants.py; existing SWA negatives remain valid for their tested setup
primary_question: Can periodic local/global attention preserve R2 capability while reducing resident KV and avoiding prior sink-eviction and dense-mask failures?
secondary_question: After separate approved training, does identity-centered head gating recover quality beyond matched all-global gate training?
invariants: Original checkpoint files, QK-Norm, MLP, RoPE, head dimensions, vocabulary and output head remain unchanged
One sequence, unpadded, no packing or beam search; original context limit only
Global layers at 3,7,11,15,19,23,27 for 28L; final layer explicitly global at other depths
Window is total local token budget including current token and any persistent sinks
Sink512 means four initial tokens plus 508 recent tokens, not 512 plus four
Absolute position identities survive KV eviction; no renumbering
2*sigmoid(W*x), W=0, is identity with a live first-order gradient
No zero-alpha AND zero-W tanh parameterization: that would kill both gradients
Native implementation is parity oracle; every research arm uses the same explicit backend
No runtime/context/speed claim from arithmetic or logical tensor shapes alone

arms.A1_local1024: period-4 local/global, window1024, no sinks or gate
arms.A2_local512: period-4 local/global, window512, no sinks or gate
arms.A3_sink512: A2 with 4 sink slots inside the same 512-slot budget
arms.A4_global_gate: A0 plus identity-initialized head gate; all-global training control later
arms.A7_sink1024: A1 with 4 sink slots inside the same 1024-slot budget

stages.P0: CPU fixture tests: dense oracle, causal masks, real storage, gates, gradients, reset and guards
stages.P1: Local checkpoint inventory; no remote downloads, no arbitrary model substitution
stages.P2: Native-vs-global logits/argmax parity, full-vs-stream equivalence, compact resident cache, gate identity
stages.P3: Only after matching P2 receipt: new open synthetic raw-completion diagnostics; no model promotion
stages.P4: CLOSED: reviewed training data/license/provenance, matched gate controls, seeds and budgets must be registered first
stages.P5: CLOSED: broader preservation/held-out confirmation and controlled hardware benchmark require separate registration

qualification.note: Tiny windows test mechanics; they do not qualify quality at 512/1024 or long-context throughput

diagnostics.prompt_protocol: raw completion, not chat template; precise token lengths, no truncation
diagnostics.decoding: greedy, max_new_tokens24, no extra repetition/abstention bias; stop at checkpoint EOS
diagnostics.comparison: paired by case ID and prompt hash; exact McNemar is descriptive and unadjusted, not confirmatory
diagnostics.gate_identity: A0=A4, A2=A5 and A3=A6 token-for-token before training; any difference invalidates the diagnostic
diagnostics.timing: descriptive only; fixed arm order, no isolation proof, no causal speed claim

future_training_requirements: Human-reviewed dataset source/license/derivation declaration and exact content hashes
Train/dev separation and duplicate/near-duplicate audit; no legacy sealed assets
Same data membership/order, supervised tokens, steps, optimizer and decoding in matched arms
Frozen backbone and gate-only parameter allowlist; all-global trained gate control
At least three registered seeds; checkpoint selection on DEV only
Independent confirmation plan with prespecified effect size, noninferiority margins and multiplicity handling
Training remains unavailable in this CLI until those requirements are implemented and reviewed
